theorem actual_centered_polar_isometry
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,

      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ)*‖v‖^2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ)*η ≤ 1) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    let Λ := J.map (fun p : E × E => (p.2,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2))
    let F := fun p : E × E => (p.1,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2)
    let mY := MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E)
    letI : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := Prod.instMeasurableSpace
    letI : Fact (mY ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (E × E))) :=
      ⟨measurable_snd.comap_le⟩
    let HP := lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J
    let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
      HP.subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (μ := J) measurable_snd.comap_le
    let hp : MeasurePreserving (Prod.snd : E × E → E) J ν := ⟨measurable_snd,rfl⟩

    HP = P.toLinearMap.range ∧
    (∀ f : HP, P (f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = f) ∧
    ∃ S : Kernel E E, IsMarkovKernel S ∧
      (∀ y, S y = (volume : Measure E).tilted
        (fun x => -V ((1/2 : ℝ) • (y+x)) - ‖y-x‖^2/(8*η))) ∧
      Λ.IsCondKernel S ∧ Λ.fst = ν ∧ Λ.snd = ν ∧

        ∃ U : Lp ℝ 2 J →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J,

          Function.Involutive U ∧ IsSelfAdjoint U.toContinuousLinearMap ∧

              ‖T u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ ∧
              (T u : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[ν] (fun y => ∫ x, u x ∂S y) ∧
              (∫ y, T u y ∂ν) = ∫ y, u y ∂ν) ∧
            let A : HP →L[ℝ] HP :=
              HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘L U.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L HP.subtypeL
            let B : HP →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
              (((1 : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J)-P)*U.toContinuousLinearMap*P) ∘L HP.subtypeL

            (∀ f : HP, ‖A f‖ ≤ ‖f‖) ∧
            (∀ f : HP, P (B f) = 0) ∧

              B.adjoint ∘L B = ΓP*ΓP ∧

                letI : NormedAddCommGroup HP0 := HP0.normedAddCommGroup
                letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP0 := HP0.innerProductSpace
                letI : CompleteSpace HP0 := (innerSL ℝ qP).isClosed_ker.completeSpace_coe
                let γ : ℝ := 2*Real.sqrt ((α : ℝ)*η)/(1+(α : ℝ)*η)

                    letI : NormedAddCommGroup Hperp := Hperp.normedAddCommGroup
                    letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ Hperp := Hperp.innerProductSpace
                    letI : CompleteSpace Hperp := P.isClosed_ker.completeSpace_coe

                      (∀ f : HP0, (B0 f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = B (f : HP)) ∧
                      ∃ V0 : HP0 →L[ℝ] Hperp,

                        V0.adjoint ∘L V0 = (1 : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0) ∧

  classical
  dsimp only
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
  let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
    (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
  let ν := J.snd
  let mY : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E)
  letI : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := Prod.instMeasurableSpace
  letI : Fact (mY ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (E × E))) := ⟨measurable_snd.comap_le⟩
  let HP := lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J
  letI : NormedAddCommGroup HP := HP.normedAddCommGroup
  letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP := HP.innerProductSpace
  let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
    HP.subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (μ := J) measurable_snd.comap_le
  have hBase := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.CenteredRootOrderInverse.actual_centered_root_order_inverse
    (E:=E) (V:=V) (α:=α) (β:=β) (η:=η) hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  dsimp only at hBase
  rcases hBase with
    ⟨hμ,hJ,hν,hRange,hPf,S,hS,hSd,hSc,hSf,hSs,e,he,U,hU,hUi,hUs,
      T,hTs,hAll,hAeq,hAs,hAn,hPB,Γ,hΓ,hΓSq,hΓP,hΓPSq,hGram,
      q,hqa,hTq,hq,hCenter,hΓPq,hγ,ΓP0,hΓP0,hPos0,hOrder0,hUnit,
      Inv,hLeft,hRight,hNormInv⟩
  let A : HP →L[ℝ] HP := HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘L U.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L HP.subtypeL
  let B : HP →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
    (((1 : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J)-P)*U.toContinuousLinearMap*P) ∘L HP.subtypeL
  let ΓP : HP →L[ℝ] HP := e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ
  let qP : HP := e q
  let HP0 := (innerSL ℝ qP).ker
  letI : NormedAddCommGroup HP0 := HP0.normedAddCommGroup
  letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP0 := HP0.innerProductSpace
  letI : CompleteSpace HP0 := (innerSL ℝ qP).isClosed_ker.completeSpace_coe
  let Hperp := P.ker
  letI : NormedAddCommGroup Hperp := Hperp.normedAddCommGroup
  letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ Hperp := Hperp.innerProductSpace
  letI : CompleteSpace Hperp := P.isClosed_ker.completeSpace_coe
  let B0 : HP0 →L[ℝ] Hperp :=
    (B ∘L HP0.subtypeL).codRestrict Hperp (by intro f; exact hPB (f : HP))
  have hB0 (f : HP0) : (B0 f : Lp ℝ 2 J)=B (f : HP) := rfl
  let V0 : HP0 →L[ℝ] Hperp := B0 ∘L Inv
  have hGramLocal : B.adjoint ∘L B=ΓP*ΓP := hGram
  have hPosLocal : ΓP.IsPositive := hΓP
  have hVnorm (f : HP0) : ‖V0 f‖=‖f‖ := by
    let g : HP0 := Inv f
    have hg : ΓP0 g=f := congrArg (fun C : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0 => C f) hRight
    have hb := B.apply_norm_sq_eq_inner_adjoint_right (g : HP)
    have hr := ΓP.apply_norm_sq_eq_inner_adjoint_right (g : HP)
    rw [hGramLocal] at hb
    rw [hPosLocal.isSelfAdjoint.adjoint_eq] at hr
    have hNorm : ‖B (g : HP)‖=‖ΓP (g : HP)‖ :=
      (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp (hb.trans hr.symm)
    calc
      ‖V0 f‖=‖B (g : HP)‖ := rfl
      _ = ‖ΓP (g : HP)‖ := hNorm
      _ = ‖ΓP0 g‖ := congrArg (fun z : HP => ‖z‖) (hΓP0 g).symm
      _ = ‖f‖ := congrArg (fun z : HP0 => ‖z‖) hg
  have hFactor : B0=V0 ∘L ΓP0 := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro f
    change B0 f=B0 (Inv (ΓP0 f))
    have hf : Inv (ΓP0 f)=f := congrArg (fun C : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0 => C f) hLeft
    rw [hf]

    (ContinuousLinearMap.norm_map_iff_adjoint_comp_self V0).mp hVnorm
  exact ⟨hμ,hJ,hν,hRange,hPf,S,hS,hSd,hSc,hSf,hSs,e,he,U,hU,hUi,hUs,T,hTs,hAll,
    hAeq,hAs,hAn,hPB,Γ,hΓ,hΓSq,hΓP,hΓPSq,hGram,q,hqa,hTq,hq,hCenter,hΓPq,hγ,
    ΓP0,hΓP0,hPos0,hOrder0,hUnit,Inv,hLeft,hRight,hNormInv,B0,hB0,V0,rfl,
    hFactor,hVadj,hVnorm⟩

end

theorem actual_centered_root_order_inverse
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}

    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ)*η ≤ 1) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    let Λ := J.map (fun p : E × E => (p.2,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2))
    let F := fun p : E × E => (p.1,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2)
    let mY := MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E)
    letI : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := Prod.instMeasurableSpace
    letI : Fact (mY ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (E × E))) :=
      ⟨measurable_snd.comap_le⟩
    let HP := lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J
    let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
      HP.subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (μ := J) measurable_snd.comap_le
    let hp : MeasurePreserving (Prod.snd : E × E → E) J ν := ⟨measurable_snd,rfl⟩
    let M : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J := Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.snd hp

    HP = P.toLinearMap.range ∧
    (∀ f : HP, P (f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = f) ∧
    ∃ S : Kernel E E, IsMarkovKernel S ∧
      (∀ y, S y = (volume : Measure E).tilted
        (fun x => -V ((1/2 : ℝ) • (y+x)) - ‖y-x‖^2/(8*η))) ∧
      Λ.IsCondKernel S ∧ Λ.fst = ν ∧ Λ.snd = ν ∧
      ∃ e : Lp ℝ 2 ν ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] HP,
        (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, (e u : Lp ℝ 2 J) = M u) ∧
        ∃ U : Lp ℝ 2 J →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J,
          (∀ g : Lp ℝ 2 J, (U g : E × E → ℝ) =ᵐ[J] g ∘ F) ∧
          Function.Involutive U ∧ IsSelfAdjoint U.toContinuousLinearMap ∧
          ∃ T : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν,
            IsSelfAdjoint T ∧

              ‖T u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ ∧
              (T u : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[ν] (fun y => ∫ x, u x ∂S y) ∧
              (∫ y, T u y ∂ν) = ∫ y, u y ∂ν) ∧
            let A : HP →L[ℝ] HP :=
              HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘L U.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L HP.subtypeL
            let B : HP →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
              (((1 : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J)-P)*U.toContinuousLinearMap*P) ∘L HP.subtypeL

            (∀ f : HP, ‖A f‖ ≤ ‖f‖) ∧
            (∀ f : HP, P (B f) = 0) ∧
            ∃ Γ : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν,
              Γ.IsPositive ∧ Γ*Γ=(1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T ∧
              let ΓP : HP →L[ℝ] HP := e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ

              B.adjoint ∘L B = ΓP*ΓP ∧
              ∃ q : Lp ℝ 2 ν,

                (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, inner ℝ q u = ∫ y, u y ∂ν) ∧
                let qP : HP := e q

                letI : NormedAddCommGroup HP0 := HP0.normedAddCommGroup
                letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP0 := HP0.innerProductSpace
                let γ : ℝ := 2*Real.sqrt ((α : ℝ)*η)/(1+(α : ℝ)*η)
                (∀ f : HP, f ∈ HP0 ↔ (∫ y, (e.symm f) y ∂ν) = 0) ∧
                ΓP qP = 0 ∧ 0 < γ ∧

                    ΓP0*Inv=(1 : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0) ∧ ‖Inv‖ ≤ 1/γ := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)

  let mY : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E)
  letI : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := Prod.instMeasurableSpace
  letI : Fact (mY ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (E × E))) := ⟨measurable_snd.comap_le⟩
  let HP := lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J
  letI : NormedAddCommGroup HP := HP.normedAddCommGroup
  letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP := HP.innerProductSpace
  let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
    HP.subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (μ := J) measurable_snd.comap_le
  have hBase := MacroscopicDefectRoot.actual_unique_positive_macroscopic_defect_root

    ⟨hμ,hJ,hν,hRange,hPf,S,hS,hSd,hSc,hSf,hSs,e,he,U,hU,hUi,hUs,

  let A : HP →L[ℝ] HP := HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘L U.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L HP.subtypeL

  let ΓP : HP →L[ℝ] HP := e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ
  have hAeqLocal : A=e.conjStarAlgEquiv T := hAeq
  let q : Lp ℝ 2 ν := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.L2Expectation.one ν
  have hq (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) : inner ℝ q u=∫ y,u y ∂ν :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.L2Expectation.inner_one_eq_integral ν u
  have hqa : (q : E → ℝ)=ᵐ[ν] (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) :=
    Lp.coeFn_const (α:=E) (μ:=ν) (p:=(2 : ℝ≥0∞)) (c:=(1 : ℝ))

    intro u

    change ‖(e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ) (e u)‖^2=‖e u‖^2-‖A (e u)‖^2 at hs
    simpa only [LinearIsometryEquiv.conjStarAlgEquiv_apply_apply,e.symm_apply_apply,
      hAction,e.norm_map] using hs
  have hΓq : Γ q=0 := by
    have h : ‖Γ q‖^2=0 := by rw [hΓEnergy,hTq,sub_self]
    exact norm_eq_zero.mp (by nlinarith [norm_nonneg (Γ q)])
  have hPIBase :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.GaussianMarginalPoincare.actual_gaussian_marginal_centered_poincare
      (E:=E) (V:=V) (α:=α) (β:=β) (η:=η) hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  dsimp only at hPIBase
  rcases hPIBase with ⟨_,G,_,hClose,hClosed,hGraph,hPI⟩
  have hRoughBase := RoughMeanGradient.actual_rough_mean_gradient
    (E:=E) (V:=V) (α:=α) (β:=β) (η:=η) hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  dsimp only at hRoughBase
  rcases hRoughBase with ⟨_,G',_,_,_,hGraph',Tr,K,hRough⟩
  have hSameG : G'=G := LinearPMap.eq_of_eq_graph (by
    ext p
    rcases p with ⟨u,v⟩
    exact (hGraph' u v).trans (hGraph u v).symm)
  subst G'

    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext

    exact hr.trans ((congrArg (fun m : Measure E => ∫ x,u x ∂m) (hSd y)).symm.trans ht.symm)
  subst Tr
  have ha0 : 0 < (α : ℝ)*η := mul_pos hα hη
  have ha1 : (α : ℝ)*η ≤ 1 :=

  let ρ : ℝ := (1-(α : ℝ)*η)/(1+(α : ℝ)*η)

    have hz : (∫ x,(z : Lp ℝ 2 ν) x ∂ν)=0 := (hAll u).2.2.trans hu

      apply (le_div_iff₀ (sq_pos_of_pos hd)).2

    exact (sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg hρ (norm_nonneg _))).mp hSq'
  let Q : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν := 1-(innerSL ℝ q).smulRight q

    simp
  have hDecomp (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) : u=Q u+inner ℝ q u • q := by rw [hQ];abel

    simp only [starRingEnd_apply,star_trivial]

    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.L2RealSquareOrder.positive_square_order

  let qP : HP := e q

  letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP0 := HP0.innerProductSpace

    rw [← e.apply_symm_apply f, e.inner_map_map,hq,e.symm_apply_apply]

    have hs : inner ℝ qP (ΓP (f : HP))=inner ℝ (ΓP qP) (f : HP) :=

    refine ⟨?_,?_⟩
    · intro f g

    apply (ContinuousLinearMap.isPositive_iff' _).mpr
    refine ⟨hPos0.isSelfAdjoint.sub ((ContinuousLinearMap.isPositive_one).smul_of_nonneg hγ.le).isSelfAdjoint,?_⟩
    intro f
    let u : Lp ℝ 2 ν := e.symm (f : HP)
    have hu : inner ℝ q u=0 := by rw [hq];exact (hCenter _).mp f.property
    have hQu : Q u=u := by rw [hQ,hu,zero_smul,sub_zero]
    have h := hOrder.inner_nonneg_left u
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply,ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply,
      ContinuousLinearMap.one_apply,inner_sub_left,inner_smul_left,hQu] at h ⊢
    have hInner : inner ℝ (ΓP0 f) f=inner ℝ (Γ u) u := by
      change inner ℝ (ΓP (f : HP)) (f : HP)=_
      change inner ℝ (e (Γ u)) (f : HP)=_
      rw [← e.apply_symm_apply (f : HP),e.inner_map_map]
    rw [hInner]
    have hNorm : inner ℝ f f=inner ℝ u u := by
      change inner ℝ (f : HP) (f : HP)=_
      rw [← e.apply_symm_apply (f : HP),e.inner_map_map]
    rw [hNorm]
    exact h

      starRingEnd_apply,star_trivial] at h

    apply ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_of_forall_le_norm_inner_map ΓP0 (c:=⟨γ,hγ.le⟩) hγ
    intro f

    exact (congrArg (fun C : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0 => C*Inv) hUnit.unit_spec).symm.trans

  have hNormCoerc (f : HP0) : γ*‖f‖ ≤ ‖ΓP0 f‖ := by

  exact ⟨hμ,hJ,hν,hRange,hPf,S,hS,hSd,hSc,hSf,hSs,e,he,U,hU,hUi,hUs,T,hTs,hAll,

end

noncomputable section

theorem actual_unique_positive_macroscopic_defect_root
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ)*‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ)*‖v‖^2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ)*η ≤ 1) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    let Λ := J.map (fun p : E × E => (p.2,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2))
    let F := fun p : E × E => (p.1,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2)
    let mY := MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E)
    letI : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := Prod.instMeasurableSpace
    letI : Fact (mY ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (E × E))) :=
      ⟨measurable_snd.comap_le⟩
    let HP := lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J
    let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
      HP.subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (μ := J) measurable_snd.comap_le
    let hp : MeasurePreserving (Prod.snd : E × E → E) J ν := ⟨measurable_snd,rfl⟩
    let M : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J := Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.snd hp
    IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure J ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
    HP = P.toLinearMap.range ∧
    (∀ f : HP, P (f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = f) ∧
    ∃ S : Kernel E E, IsMarkovKernel S ∧
      (∀ y, S y = (volume : Measure E).tilted
        (fun x => -V ((1/2 : ℝ) • (y+x)) - ‖y-x‖^2/(8*η))) ∧
      Λ.IsCondKernel S ∧ Λ.fst = ν ∧ Λ.snd = ν ∧
      ∃ e : Lp ℝ 2 ν ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] HP,
        (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, (e u : Lp ℝ 2 J) = M u) ∧
        ∃ U : Lp ℝ 2 J →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J,
          (∀ g : Lp ℝ 2 J, (U g : E × E → ℝ) =ᵐ[J] g ∘ F) ∧
          Function.Involutive U ∧ IsSelfAdjoint U.toContinuousLinearMap ∧
          ∃ T : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν,
            IsSelfAdjoint T ∧
            (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν,
              ‖T u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ ∧
              (T u : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[ν] (fun y => ∫ x, u x ∂S y) ∧
              (∫ y, T u y ∂ν) = ∫ y, u y ∂ν) ∧
            let A : HP →L[ℝ] HP :=
              HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘L U.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L HP.subtypeL
            let B : HP →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
              (((1 : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J)-P)*U.toContinuousLinearMap*P) ∘L HP.subtypeL
            A = e.conjStarAlgEquiv T ∧ IsSelfAdjoint A ∧
            (∀ f : HP, ‖A f‖ ≤ ‖f‖) ∧
            (∀ f : HP, P (B f) = 0) ∧
            ∃ Γ : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν,
              Γ.IsPositive ∧ Γ*Γ=(1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T ∧
              let ΓP : HP →L[ℝ] HP := e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ
              ΓP.IsPositive ∧ ΓP*ΓP=(1 : HP →L[ℝ] HP)-A*A ∧
              B.adjoint ∘L B = ΓP*ΓP ∧
              (∀ f : HP, ‖B f‖ = ‖ΓP f‖ ∧
                ‖ΓP f‖^2 = ‖f‖^2-‖A f‖^2) ∧
              (∀ G : HP →L[ℝ] HP,
                G.IsPositive → G*G=(1 : HP →L[ℝ] HP)-A*A → G=ΓP)
:= by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
  let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
    (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
  let ν := J.snd
  let mY : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E)
  letI : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := Prod.instMeasurableSpace
  letI : Fact (mY ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (E × E))) :=
    ⟨measurable_snd.comap_le⟩
  let HP := lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J
  letI : NormedAddCommGroup HP := HP.normedAddCommGroup
  letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP := HP.innerProductSpace
  let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
    HP.subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (μ := J) measurable_snd.comap_le
  let hp : MeasurePreserving (Prod.snd : E × E → E) J ν := ⟨measurable_snd,rfl⟩
  let M : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J := Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.snd hp
  rcases CenteredDefectOperator.actual_centered_selfadjoint_defect hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη with
    ⟨hμ,hJ,hν,S,hS,hSd,hSc,hSf,hSs,U,hU,hUi,hUs,M0,hM0,T,hTs,hAll,
      q,hqa,hTq,hqi,hzero,hD,hDq,hDef,hRest⟩
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure J := hJ
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := hν
  have hM0eq : M0 = M := by
    apply LinearIsometry.ext
    intro u
    apply Lp.ext
    exact (hM0 u).trans (Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving u hp).symm
  subst M0
  have hPdef : P = HP.starProjection := rfl
  have hPrange : P.toLinearMap.range = HP := by
    change P.range = HP
    rw [hPdef]
    exact HP.range_starProjection
  have hMR : M.toLinearMap.range = P.toLinearMap.range :=
    (MacroscopicRange.actual_macroscopic_centered_range hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη).2.2.1
  let e : Lp ℝ 2 ν ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] HP :=
    M.equivRange.trans (LinearIsometryEquiv.ofEq _ _ (hMR.trans hPrange))
  have he (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) : (e u : Lp ℝ 2 J) = M u := rfl
  have hPf (f : HP) : P (f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = f := by
    rw [hPdef]
    exact HP.starProjection_mem_subspace_eq_self f
  have hPP : P*P=P := by rw [hPdef];exact HP.isIdempotentElem_starProjection
  have hPid (f : Lp ℝ 2 J) : P (P f)=P f := by
    change (P*P) f=P f
    rw [hPP]
  let A : HP →L[ℝ] HP :=
    HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘L U.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L HP.subtypeL
  let B0 : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
    ((1 : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J)-P)*U.toContinuousLinearMap*P
  let AJ := P*U.toContinuousLinearMap*P
  let B : HP →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J := B0 ∘L HP.subtypeL
  have hAincl (f : HP) : (A f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = AJ f := by
    change P (U f) = P (U (P f))
    rw [hPf]
  have hAeq : A=e.conjStarAlgEquiv T := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro f
    apply Subtype.ext
    change (A f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = (e (T (e.symm f)) : Lp ℝ 2 J)
    rw [hAincl,he]
    have hf : M (e.symm f) = (f : Lp ℝ 2 J) := by
      rw [← he,e.apply_symm_apply]
    rw [← hf]
    exact ((hAll (e.symm f)).2.1).symm
  have hAapply (f : HP) : A f=e (T (e.symm f)) := by rw [hAeq];rfl
  have hAs : IsSelfAdjoint A := by
    rw [hAeq]
    simpa only [LinearIsometryEquiv.conjStarAlgEquiv_apply,e.adjoint_eq_symm] using
      hTs.conj_adjoint (e : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] HP)
  have hAn (f : HP) : ‖A f‖ ≤ ‖f‖ := by
    rw [hAapply,e.norm_map]
    exact ((hAll (e.symm f)).2.2.1).trans_eq (e.symm.norm_map f)
  have hPB (f : HP) : P (B f)=0 := by
    change P (U (P f)-P (U (P f)))=0
    rw [map_sub,hPid,sub_self]
  obtain ⟨R,hR,hRf,U2,hU2,hU2i,hU2s,hRp,hBB,hBD,hBE⟩ :=
    ReflectionL2.actual_reflection_block_identities μ hη
  have hU2eq : U2=U := by
    apply LinearIsometry.ext
    intro f
    apply Lp.ext
    exact (hU2 f).trans (hU f).symm
  subst U2
  have hB0Gram : B0.adjoint ∘L B0=P-AJ*AJ := by
    have hBBtyped : B0.adjoint ∘L B0 = P-AJ^2 := hBB
    simpa only [pow_two] using hBBtyped
  obtain ⟨Γ,hΓ,hΓSq,hEnergy⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.L2RealSquareRoot.exists_positive_real_square_root
      ν ((1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T) hD
  let ΓP : HP →L[ℝ] HP := e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ
  have hΓP : ΓP.IsPositive := by
    simpa only [ΓP,LinearIsometryEquiv.conjStarAlgEquiv_apply,e.adjoint_eq_symm] using
      hΓ.conj_adjoint (e : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] HP)
  have hΓPSq : ΓP*ΓP=(1 : HP →L[ℝ] HP)-A*A := by
    change e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ*e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ=_
    rw [← map_mul,hΓSq,map_sub,map_one,map_mul,← hAeq]
  have hGram : B.adjoint ∘L B=ΓP*ΓP := by
    calc
      B.adjoint ∘L B = HP.subtypeL.adjoint ∘L (B0.adjoint ∘L B0) ∘L HP.subtypeL := by
        simp only [B,ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp,ContinuousLinearMap.comp_assoc]
      _ = HP.subtypeL.adjoint ∘L (P-AJ*AJ) ∘L HP.subtypeL := by rw [hB0Gram]
      _ = (1 : HP →L[ℝ] HP)-A*A := by
        apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
        intro f
        rw [HP.adjoint_subtypeL]
        change HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto (P f-AJ (AJ f))=f-A (A f)
        rw [hPf,← hAincl f,← hAincl (A f),map_sub]
        simp only [Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_mem_subspace_eq_self]
      _ = ΓP*ΓP := hΓPSq.symm
  have hMacroEnergy (f : HP) : ‖ΓP f‖^2=‖f‖^2-‖A f‖^2 := by
    have hs : ‖Γ (e.symm f)‖^2=‖e.symm f‖^2-‖T (e.symm f)‖^2 :=
      (hEnergy (e.symm f)).trans (hDef (e.symm f))
    simpa only [ΓP,LinearIsometryEquiv.conjStarAlgEquiv_apply_apply,hAapply,
      e.norm_map,e.symm.norm_map] using hs
  have hNorm (f : HP) : ‖B f‖=‖ΓP f‖ := by
    have hb := B.apply_norm_sq_eq_inner_adjoint_right f
    have hg := ΓP.apply_norm_sq_eq_inner_adjoint_right f
    rw [hGram] at hb
    rw [hΓP.isSelfAdjoint.adjoint_eq] at hg
    exact (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp (hb.trans hg.symm)
  have hUnique (G : HP →L[ℝ] HP) (hG : G.IsPositive)
      (hGSq : G*G=(1 : HP →L[ℝ] HP)-A*A) : G=ΓP := by
    let G0 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν := e.symm.conjStarAlgEquiv G
    have hG0 : G0.IsPositive := by
      simpa only [G0,LinearIsometryEquiv.conjStarAlgEquiv_apply,e.symm.adjoint_eq_symm] using
        hG.conj_adjoint (e.symm : HP →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)
    have hPullA : e.symm.conjStarAlgEquiv A=T := by
      rw [hAeq]
      apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
      intro u
      simp only [LinearIsometryEquiv.conjStarAlgEquiv_apply_apply,
        LinearIsometryEquiv.symm_symm,e.symm_apply_apply,e.apply_symm_apply]
    have hG0Sq : G0*G0=(1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T := by
      change e.symm.conjStarAlgEquiv G*e.symm.conjStarAlgEquiv G=_
      rw [← map_mul,hGSq,map_sub,map_one,map_mul,hPullA]
    have hEq : G0=Γ :=
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.L2RealSquareRootUnique.positive_square_roots_unique
        ν G0 Γ hG0 hΓ (hG0Sq.trans hΓSq.symm)
    calc
      G=e.conjStarAlgEquiv G0 := by
        apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
        intro f
        simp only [G0,LinearIsometryEquiv.conjStarAlgEquiv_apply_apply,
          LinearIsometryEquiv.symm_symm,e.symm_apply_apply,e.apply_symm_apply]
      _ = e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ := congrArg e.conjStarAlgEquiv hEq
      _ = ΓP := rfl
  refine ⟨hμ,hJ,hν,hPrange.symm,hPf,S,hS,hSd,hSc,hSf,hSs,e,he,U,hU,hUi,hUs,
    T,hTs,?_,hAeq,hAs,hAn,hPB,Γ,hΓ,hΓSq,hΓP,hΓPSq,hGram,?_,hUnique⟩
  · intro u
    exact (hAll u).2.2
  · intro f
    exact ⟨hNorm f,hMacroEnergy f⟩

end
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.MacroscopicDefectRoot

theorem actual_centered_polar_isometry
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ)*‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ)*‖v‖^2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ)*η ≤ 1) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    let Λ := J.map (fun p : E × E => (p.2,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2))
    let F := fun p : E × E => (p.1,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2)
    let mY := MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E)
    letI : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := Prod.instMeasurableSpace
    letI : Fact (mY ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (E × E))) :=
      ⟨measurable_snd.comap_le⟩
    let HP := lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J
    let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
      HP.subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (μ := J) measurable_snd.comap_le
    let hp : MeasurePreserving (Prod.snd : E × E → E) J ν := ⟨measurable_snd,rfl⟩
    let M : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J := Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.snd hp
    IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure J ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
    HP = P.toLinearMap.range ∧
    (∀ f : HP, P (f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = f) ∧
    ∃ S : Kernel E E, IsMarkovKernel S ∧
      (∀ y, S y = (volume : Measure E).tilted
        (fun x => -V ((1/2 : ℝ) • (y+x)) - ‖y-x‖^2/(8*η))) ∧
      Λ.IsCondKernel S ∧ Λ.fst = ν ∧ Λ.snd = ν ∧
      ∃ e : Lp ℝ 2 ν ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] HP,
        (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, (e u : Lp ℝ 2 J) = M u) ∧
        ∃ U : Lp ℝ 2 J →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J,
          (∀ g : Lp ℝ 2 J, (U g : E × E → ℝ) =ᵐ[J] g ∘ F) ∧
          Function.Involutive U ∧ IsSelfAdjoint U.toContinuousLinearMap ∧
          ∃ T : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν,
            IsSelfAdjoint T ∧
            (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν,
              ‖T u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ ∧
              (T u : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[ν] (fun y => ∫ x, u x ∂S y) ∧
              (∫ y, T u y ∂ν) = ∫ y, u y ∂ν) ∧
            let A : HP →L[ℝ] HP :=
              HP.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘L U.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L HP.subtypeL
            let B : HP →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
              (((1 : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J)-P)*U.toContinuousLinearMap*P) ∘L HP.subtypeL
            A = e.conjStarAlgEquiv T ∧ IsSelfAdjoint A ∧
            (∀ f : HP, ‖A f‖ ≤ ‖f‖) ∧
            (∀ f : HP, P (B f) = 0) ∧
            ∃ Γ : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν,
              Γ.IsPositive ∧ Γ*Γ=(1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T ∧
              let ΓP : HP →L[ℝ] HP := e.conjStarAlgEquiv Γ
              ΓP.IsPositive ∧ ΓP*ΓP=(1 : HP →L[ℝ] HP)-A*A ∧
              B.adjoint ∘L B = ΓP*ΓP ∧
              ∃ q : Lp ℝ 2 ν,
                (q : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[ν] (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ∧ T q = q ∧
                (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, inner ℝ q u = ∫ y, u y ∂ν) ∧
                let qP : HP := e q
                let HP0 := (innerSL ℝ qP).ker
                letI : NormedAddCommGroup HP0 := HP0.normedAddCommGroup
                letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP0 := HP0.innerProductSpace
                letI : CompleteSpace HP0 := (innerSL ℝ qP).isClosed_ker.completeSpace_coe
                let γ : ℝ := 2*Real.sqrt ((α : ℝ)*η)/(1+(α : ℝ)*η)
                (∀ f : HP, f ∈ HP0 ↔ (∫ y, (e.symm f) y ∂ν) = 0) ∧
                ΓP qP = 0 ∧ 0 < γ ∧
                ∃ ΓP0 : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0,
                  (∀ f : HP0, (ΓP0 f : HP) = ΓP (f : HP)) ∧
                  ΓP0.IsPositive ∧ (ΓP0-γ • (1 : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0)).IsPositive ∧
                  IsUnit ΓP0 ∧
                  ∃ Inv : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0,
                    Inv*ΓP0=(1 : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0) ∧
                    ΓP0*Inv=(1 : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0) ∧ ‖Inv‖ ≤ 1/γ ∧
                    let Hperp := P.ker
                    letI : NormedAddCommGroup Hperp := Hperp.normedAddCommGroup
                    letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ Hperp := Hperp.innerProductSpace
                    letI : CompleteSpace Hperp := P.isClosed_ker.completeSpace_coe
                    ∃ B0 : HP0 →L[ℝ] Hperp,
                      (∀ f : HP0, (B0 f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = B (f : HP)) ∧
                      ∃ V0 : HP0 →L[ℝ] Hperp,
                        V0 = B0 ∘L Inv ∧ B0 = V0 ∘L ΓP0 ∧
                        V0.adjoint ∘L V0 = (1 : HP0 →L[ℝ] HP0) ∧
                        (∀ f : HP0, ‖V0 f‖ = ‖f‖)

finite_exact_RAW_inputs.utf8:
1 Introduction

We study the problem of sampling from the probability measure μ⁡(d​x)=Z−1​e−V⁡(x)​d​x\mu(\mathrm{d}x)=Z^{-1}e^{-V(x)}\,\mathrm{d}x on ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}, where V∈C2​(ℝd)V\in C^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d}) satisfies, for 0<α≤β0<\alpha\leq\beta,

α​I⪯∇2V​(x)⪯β​I,x∈ℝd,κ≔βα.\alpha I\preceq\nabla^{2}V(x)\preceq\beta I\,,\hskip 20.00003ptx\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\kappa\coloneqq\tfrac{\beta}{\alpha}\,. (1.1)

The main result of this paper is the following.

Theorem (Main theorem; informal).

Assume (1.1), and suppose that the initial law μ0\mu_{0} satisfies the warm start condition in order-22 Rényi divergence: D2(μ0∥μ)=O(1)D_{2}(\mu_{0}\|\mu)=O(1). For every 0<ε<1/40<\varepsilon<1/4, there is a randomized algorithm that, given X0∼μ0X_{0}\sim\mu_{0} and query access to ∇V\nabla V, returns X^∼μ^\widehat{X}\sim\widehat{\mu} satisfying

TV⁡(μ^,μ)≤ε,\operatorname{TV}(\widehat{\mu},\mu)\leq\varepsilon\,,

and whose expected number of queries to ∇V\nabla V is at most

O~​(κ​d1/4).\widetilde{O}\bigl(\sqrt{\kappa}\,d^{1/4}\bigr)\,.

Here O~\widetilde{O} hides universal powers of logarithms in dd, κ\kappa, and 1/ε1/\varepsilon.

The precise statement and parameter choices appear in Theorems 4.3 and 4.4.

We compare our result with high-accuracy samplers, that is, samplers whose complexity depends polylogarithmically on 1/ε1/\varepsilon. Under (1.1), the state of the art until recently was the Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm (MALA) [1, 10, 27] and the proximal sampler [6, 15], which achieved O~​(κ​d1/2)\widetilde{O}(\kappa d^{1/2}) complexity. Very recently, Chen et al. [8] used the first-order rejection sampling (FORS) mechanism to develop a method for exact simulation of diffusions. Together with accelerated entropic hypocoercivity [19, 22], this yielded a high-accuracy sampler with complexity O~​(κ2/3​d1/3)\widetilde{O}(\kappa^{2/3}d^{1/3}). Also, Lu and Luo [20] introduced windowed thinning, an exact simulation method for the bouncy particle sampler (BPS) and the zigzag sampler. Their estimates give expected complexities of O~​(κ1/2​d)\widetilde{O}(\kappa^{1/2}d) gradient queries for BPS and O~​(κ​d5/4)\widetilde{O}(\kappa d^{5/4}) partial derivative queries for zigzag, from a warm start. These results were significant in part because they constituted progress toward acceleration for log-concave sampling.

From a warm start, our main theorem achieves complexity O~​(κ1/2​d1/4)\widetilde{O}(\kappa^{1/2}d^{1/4}). It matches the condition number dependence of BPS while improving its dimension dependence, and always improves upon the computational cost of the zigzag sampler (even if we consider one gradient query to be dd times as expensive as a partial derivative query). It also improves over all other prior results in both parameters. In particular, it achieves full acceleration together with d1/4d^{1/4} dependence on dimension.

In a companion work [7], we will show how to obtain a warm start using O~​(κ7/6​d1/6)\widetilde{O}(\kappa^{7/6}d^{1/6}) gradient queries. We do not discuss the warm start question further in this paper.

Proximal Bouncy Particle Sampler.

Our algorithm, the Proximal Bouncy Particle Sampler (Proximal BPS), combines two ideas. The proximal sampler [17] breaks the sampling problem into a sequence of easier local problems by introducing a Gaussian perturbation of the current position. The bouncy particle sampler [5] explores a distribution by moving a particle along straight lines, with random changes of direction chosen to preserve the desired distribution. We bring these ideas together by designing local particle motions that retain a memory of previous steps. This memory acts as momentum, allowing the algorithm to make sustained progress across successive local problems and giving the accelerated convergence rate in our main theorem. The local motions follow explicitly computable curved paths, with occasional “bounces” that correct for the shape of the target distribution. A gradient evaluation at a nearby reference point makes these corrections inexpensive: since the gradient varies little over a small region, only a small number of bounces is needed. Balancing the size of the local problems against the cost of these corrections yields the O~​(κ1/2​d1/4)\widetilde{O}(\kappa^{1/2}d^{1/4}) query bound. We feel that the construction of the sampler (with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol) contains some surprising ingredients. We describe the construction and its geometry in Section 3.1, and give the implementation and complexity analysis in Section 4.

Related work.

This work makes progress on the complexity of log-concave sampling, for which the textbook [11] provides an introduction and overview.

The proximal sampling framework is from Lee, Shen, and Tian [17], with subsequent analyses and implementations in [6, 9, 15]. These methods alternate independent draws of the position and the auxiliary variable from their conditional distributions. Our update reflects the auxiliary point through the current position, a step related to the Gaussian overrelaxation method of Neal [25]. We combine this reflection with a local piecewise deterministic particle motion run for half of its oscillation period. As we shall explain, this helps useful information to persist across iterations.

The rule for the bounces builds on the BPS of Bouchard-Côté, Vollmer, and Doucet [5]. The use of a quadratic reference potential to generate curved paths, with bounces correcting for the remaining force, is adapted from the boomerang sampler of Bierkens, Grazzi, Kamatani, and Roberts [4]. This separation of the force also fits the general framework for Hamiltonian piecewise deterministic Markov processes of Andrieu, Durmus, Nüsken, and Roussel [2].

Existing convergence analyses of these processes [2, 13, 21] concern continuous-time dynamics with repeated random refreshment of the velocity. Our local motion has no such refreshment: it stops after a half-period, and convergence comes from combining it with the auxiliary reflection step with occasional resampling. In particular, the local motion alone need not converge to its conditional equilibrium. Thus, the continuous-time results do not directly give a convergence guarantee for our discrete chain. Our analysis instead adapts the modified L2L^{2} hypocoercivity method of Dolbeault, Mouhot, and Schmeiser [14], in the sharpened formulation of Fan, Li, and Lu [16], to this discrete setting. The technical details of the hypocoercivity mechanism in Appendices B and C should be of interest to specialists.

AI usage.

The algorithm and its original analysis were found by interactions with GPT-5.6 Sol. The authors recast the arguments into a more standard hypocoercive framework, prepared the manuscript, and take full responsibility for its contents.

2.2 Proximal augmentation and the restricted Gaussian oracle

Our algorithm operates on the augmented distribution underlying the proximal sampler of Lee, Shen, and Tian [17]. For a scale η∈(0,1/β]\eta\in(0,1/\beta], consider the joint law

πη​(d​x​d​y)∝exp⁡{−V⁡(x)−‖x−y‖22​η}​d​x​d​y.\pi_{\eta}(\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y)\propto\exp\Bigl\{-V(x)-\frac{\|x-y\|^{2}}{2\eta}\Bigr\}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y\,. (2.6)

The original proximal sampler algorithm performs Gibbs sampling on πη\pi_{\eta}. Namely, under πη\pi_{\eta} one may generate the joint state as

X∼μ,Z∼𝒩⁡(0,I)​independently,Y=X+η​Z.X\sim\mu\,,\hskip 20.00003ptZ\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)\ \text{independently}\,,\hskip 20.00003ptY=X+\sqrt{\eta}\,Z\,. (2.7)

Its XX-marginal is πηX=μ\pi_{\eta}^{X}=\mu. Write πηY\pi_{\eta}^{Y} for the YY-marginal, so that πηY​(d​y)∝e−Uη​(y)​d​y\pi_{\eta}^{Y}(\mathrm{d}y)\propto e^{-U_{\eta}(y)}\,\mathrm{d}y; by (2.7), πηY=μ∗𝒩⁡(0,η​I)\pi_{\eta}^{Y}=\mu*\mathcal{N}(0,\eta I) is a Gaussian smoothing of the target. We use superscripts for marginal and conditional laws; in particular,

πηY|X=x=𝒩⁡(x,η​I),πηX|Y=y​(d​x)∝exp⁡{−V⁡(x)−‖x−y‖22​η}​d​x.\pi_{\eta}^{Y\mid X=x}=\mathcal{N}(x,\eta I)\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y}(\mathrm{d}x)\propto\exp\Bigl\{-V(x)-\frac{\|x-y\|^{2}}{2\eta}\Bigr\}\,\mathrm{d}x\,. (2.8)

Gibbs sampling alternates exact draws from the two conditional laws in (2.8). The scale η\eta controls the strength of the quadratic coupling potential. Decreasing η\eta makes XX and YY more tightly coupled and the conditional law of XX given YY more localized and better conditioned, which reduces the cost of conditional sampling. The resulting transitions are also more local, however, and generally require more Gibbs sampling iterations. Thus η\eta balances the cost of each iteration against the number of iterations. The convergence and query complexity are studied further in [6, 9, 15].

The next proposition collects the basic geometric properties of the augmented distribution used throughout the paper: the curvature and concentration of the conditional law, the curvature of the YY-marginal, and a reflection symmetry of the joint law.

Proposition 2.1 (Geometry of the joint law).

The joint law (2.6) has the following properties.

  1. (i)

    For every y∈ℝdy\in\mathbb{R}^{d}, the conditional law πηX|Y=y\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y} has potential (that is, negative log-density up to an additive constant)

    Vy​(x)≔V⁡(x)+‖x−y‖22​η.V_{y}(x)\coloneqq V(x)+\frac{\|x-y\|^{2}}{2\eta}\,. (2.9)

    This conditional potential satisfies

    (α+η−1)​I⪯∇2Vy​(x)⪯(β+η−1)​I,(\alpha+\eta^{-1})I\preceq\nabla^{2}V_{y}(x)\preceq(\beta+\eta^{-1})I\,, (2.10)

    so its condition number is at most (1+β​η)/(1+α​η)≤2(1+\beta\eta)/(1+\alpha\eta)\leq 2. Consequently, for every smooth ff,

    VarπηX|Y=y⁡(f)≤η1+α​η​𝔼πηX|Y=y​‖∇f‖2,\Var_{\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y}}(f)\leq\frac{\eta}{1+\alpha\eta}\,\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y}}\|\nabla f\|^{2}\,, (2.11)

    and

    η1+β​η​I⪯CovπηX|Y=y​(X)⪯η1+α​η​I.\frac{\eta}{1+\beta\eta}I\preceq\mathrm{Cov}_{\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y}}(X)\preceq\frac{\eta}{1+\alpha\eta}I\,. (2.12)
  2. (ii)

    The YY-marginal potential satisfies

    α1+α​η​I⪯∇2Uη​(y)⪯β1+β​η​I.\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha\eta}I\preceq\nabla^{2}U_{\eta}(y)\preceq\frac{\beta}{1+\beta\eta}I\,. (2.13)
  3. (iii)

Definition 2.2 (Restricted Gaussian oracle).

Thus 𝒦\mathcal{K} acts on probability laws, whereas 𝖪\mathsf{K} is its induced action on observables. The first term in brackets in 𝒦\mathcal{K} is the conditional resampling branch. After the auxiliary coordinate is updated to y′y^{\prime}, this branch replaces the xx-coordinate by an independent draw from πηX|Y=y′\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y^{\prime}}. Thus functions in ℌ𝖯\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P}} depend only on the coordinate yy, whereas functions in ℌ⟂\mathfrak{H}_{\perp} have zero mean under πηX|Y=y\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y} for πηY\pi_{\eta}^{Y}-almost every yy.

Relative to the decomposition ℌ=ℌ𝖯⊕ℌ⟂\mathfrak{H}=\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P}}\oplus\mathfrak{H}_{\perp}, we write an operator 𝖳\mathsf{T} on ℌ\mathfrak{H} in block form as

𝖳=(𝖳𝖯𝖯𝖳𝖯⟂𝖳⟂𝖯𝖳⟂⁣⟂),𝖳𝖯𝖯≔𝖯𝖳𝖯,𝖳𝖯⟂≔𝖯𝖳𝖯⟂,𝖳⟂𝖯≔𝖯⟂​𝖳𝖯,𝖳⟂⁣⟂≔𝖯⟂​𝖳𝖯⟂.\mathsf{T}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathsf{T}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}&\mathsf{T}_{\mathsf{P}\perp}\\ \mathsf{T}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}&\mathsf{T}_{\perp\perp}\end{pmatrix}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\begin{aligned} \mathsf{T}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}&\coloneqq\mathsf{P}\mathsf{T}\mathsf{P}\,,&\mathsf{T}_{\mathsf{P}\perp}&\coloneqq\mathsf{P}\mathsf{T}\mathsf{P}^{\perp}\,,\\ \mathsf{T}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}&\coloneqq\mathsf{P}^{\perp}\mathsf{T}\mathsf{P}\,,&\mathsf{T}_{\perp\perp}&\coloneqq\mathsf{P}^{\perp}\mathsf{T}\mathsf{P}^{\perp}\,.\end{aligned} (B.3)

We begin with the reflection operator 𝖴\mathsf{U}. Let f∈ℌ𝖯f\in\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P}}, so that f⁡(x,y)=f⁡(y)f(x,y)=f(y). Although ff initially depends only on the auxiliary coordinate yy, reflection gives (𝖴​f)​(x,y)=f⁡(2​x−y)(\mathsf{U}f)(x,y)=f(2x-y), which generally depends on both coordinates. Its macroscopic and microscopic components are 𝖴𝖯𝖯​f\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}f and 𝖴⟂𝖯​f\mathsf{U}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}f, respectively. The following probabilistic representation identifies the squared norm of the microscopic component created by reflection with an expected conditional variance, thereby enabling quantitative estimate by the conditional Poincaré estimates used in Appendix C.

Concretely, under πη\pi_{\eta}, write

Y+≔X+η​Z,Y−≔X−η​Z,Z∼𝒩⁡(0,I),X∼μ.Y_{+}\coloneqq X+\sqrt{\eta}\,Z\,,\hskip 20.00003ptY_{-}\coloneqq X-\sqrt{\eta}\,Z\,,\hskip 20.00003ptZ\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)\,,\hskip 20.00003ptX\sim\mu\,. (B.8)

To quantify the microscopic component 𝖴⟂𝖯​f\mathsf{U}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}f created when reflection acts on f∈ℌ𝖯f\in\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P}}, define

Γ𝖯≔(I−𝖴𝖯𝖯2)1/2on ​ℌ𝖯.\mathsf{\Gamma}_{\mathsf{P}}\coloneqq(I-\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}^{2})^{1/2}\hskip 10.00002pt\text{on }\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P}}\,. (B.10)

By (B.5), 𝖴⟂𝖯∗​𝖴⟂𝖯=I−𝖴𝖯𝖯2\mathsf{U}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}^{*}\mathsf{U}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}=I-\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}^{2}, and hence

𝖴⟂𝖯∗​𝖴⟂𝖯=Γ𝖯2,‖𝖴⟂𝖯​f‖=‖Γ𝖯​f‖,f∈ℌ𝖯.\mathsf{U}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}^{*}\mathsf{U}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}=\mathsf{\Gamma}_{\mathsf{P}}^{2}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\|\mathsf{U}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}f\|=\|\mathsf{\Gamma}_{\mathsf{P}}f\|\,,\hskip 10.00002ptf\in\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P}}\,. (B.11)

Lemma B.1 (Uniform macroscopic coercivity).

Assume β​η≤1\beta\eta\leq 1, and set

ρmac≔1−α​η1+α​η,γgap≔1−ρmac2=2​α​η1+α​η.\rho_{\rm mac}\coloneqq\frac{1-\alpha\eta}{1+\alpha\eta}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\gamma_{\rm gap}\coloneqq\sqrt{1-\rho_{\rm mac}^{2}}=\frac{2\sqrt{\alpha\eta}}{1+\alpha\eta}\,. (B.12)

(1) For every f∈L2​(πηY)f\in L^{2}(\pi_{\eta}^{Y}), 𝖴𝖯𝖯​f∈H1​(πηY)\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}f\in H^{1}(\pi_{\eta}^{Y}) and

4η∥∇𝖴𝖯𝖯f∥2≤∥f∥2−∥𝖴𝖯𝖯f∥2=∥Γ𝖯f∥2=∥𝖴⟂𝖯f∥2.4\eta\,\|\nabla\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}f\|^{2}\leq\|f\|^{2}-\|\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}f\|^{2}=\|\mathsf{\Gamma}_{\mathsf{P}}f\|^{2}=\|\mathsf{U}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}f\|^{2}\,. (B.13)

‖𝖴𝖯𝖯‖≤ρmacand𝖴𝖯𝖯⪰−12​Ion ​ℌ𝖯,0.\|\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}\|\leq\rho_{\rm mac}\hskip 10.00002pt\text{and}\hskip 10.00002pt\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}\succeq-\frac{1}{2}\,I\hskip 20.00003pt\text{on }\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P},0}\,. (B.14)

Γ𝖯=(I−𝖴𝖯𝖯2)1/2⪰γgap​Ion ​ℌ𝖯,0.\mathsf{\Gamma}_{\mathsf{P}}=(I-\mathsf{U}_{\mathsf{P}\mathsf{P}}^{2})^{1/2}\succeq\gamma_{\rm gap}I\hskip 20.00003pt\text{on }\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P},0}\,. (B.15)

(B.16)

Here Γ𝖯\mathsf{\Gamma}_{\mathsf{P}} measures the size of the microscopic component created by reflection, while the isometry 𝖵⟂𝖯\mathsf{V}_{\perp\mathsf{P}} records its direction in ℌ⟂\mathfrak{H}_{\perp}. The next proposition says that the half-turn acts nearly as −I-I on the corresponding microscopic directions 𝖵⟂𝖯​Γ𝖯−1​f\mathsf{V}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}\mathsf{\Gamma}_{\mathsf{P}}^{-1}f.

Proposition B.2 (Global half-turn bound).

There exist universal constants c,C>0c,C>0 such that, if β​η≤c\beta\eta\leq c, then

‖(I+𝖧⟂⁣⟂)​𝖵⟂𝖯​v‖2≤C​log⁡(1/γgap)​‖Γ𝖯​v‖2,v∈ℌ𝖯,0.\bigl\|(I+\mathsf{H}_{\perp\perp})\mathsf{V}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}v\bigr\|^{2}\leq C\log(1/\gamma_{\rm gap})\,\|\mathsf{\Gamma}_{\mathsf{P}}v\|^{2}\,,\hskip 20.00003ptv\in\mathfrak{H}_{\mathsf{P},0}\,. (B.17)

B.3 Modified L2L^{2} contraction and proof of the main theorem

We now prove Theorem 3.5 using a discrete modified L2L^{2} argument. For f∈L02​(πη)f\in L_{0}^{2}(\pi_{\eta}), write

f𝖯≔𝖯​f,f⟂≔𝖯⟂​f.f_{\mathsf{P}}\coloneqq\mathsf{P}f\,,\hskip 20.00003ptf_{\perp}\coloneqq\mathsf{P}^{\perp}f\,.

Here f𝖯f_{\mathsf{P}} and f⟂f_{\perp} are, respectively, the macroscopic and microscopic parts of ff.

Fix 0<ρ≤1/20<\rho\leq 1/2. The ordinary L2L^{2} energy does not by itself give the required one-step contraction. Indeed, since 𝖴\mathsf{U} is unitary and 𝖧⟂⁣⟂\mathsf{H}_{\perp\perp} is a contraction,

‖𝖪​f‖2−‖f‖2\displaystyle\|\mathsf{K}f\|^{2}-\|f\|^{2} =(1−ρ)2​‖𝖧⟂⁣⟂​f⟂‖2−‖f⟂‖2\displaystyle=(1-\rho)^{2}\,\|\mathsf{H}_{\perp\perp}f_{\perp}\|^{2}-\|f_{\perp}\|^{2}
≤−ρ⁡(2−ρ)​‖f⟂‖2≤−ρ​‖f⟂‖2.\displaystyle\leq-\rho\,(2-\rho)\,\|f_{\perp}\|^{2}\leq-\rho\,\|f_{\perp}\|^{2}\,. (B.18)

This estimate controls f⟂f_{\perp} but gives nothing when f=f𝖯f=f_{\mathsf{P}}. Reflection moves part of f𝖯f_{\mathsf{P}} into the microscopic subspace, but this transfer is not captured by the L2L^{2} norm, which is a standard difficulty in hypocoercivity. The modified L2L^{2} method addresses this difficulty by adding a corrector to the Lyapunov function. The corrector records the transfer from f𝖯f_{\mathsf{P}} to f⟂f_{\perp}, allowing the contraction in (B.18) to also control f𝖯f_{\mathsf{P}}. This idea goes back to Dolbeault, Mouhot, and Schmeiser [14]; here we follow the refinement of Fan, Li, and Lu [16].

To construct the corrector, we first isolate the part of f⟂f_{\perp} that couples to f𝖯f_{\mathsf{P}} under reflection. Define

f𝖵≔𝖵⟂𝖯∗​f⟂.f_{\mathsf{V}}\coloneqq\mathsf{V}_{\perp\mathsf{P}}^{*}f_{\perp}\,.

D.1 Hilbert space and Markov operator conventions

Definition D.1 (Hilbert space notation).

Let ζ\zeta be a probability measure. The real Hilbert space L2​(ζ)L^{2}(\zeta) consists of equivalence classes of measurable functions ff such that ∫f2​𝑑ζ<∞\int f^{2}\,\mathrm{d}\zeta<\infty. Its inner product and norm are

⟨f,g⟩L2​(ζ)≔∫f​g​𝑑ζ,‖f‖L2​(ζ)≔⟨f,f⟩L2​(ζ)1/2.\langle f,g\rangle_{L^{2}(\zeta)}\coloneqq\int fg\,\mathrm{d}\zeta\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\|f\|_{L^{2}(\zeta)}\coloneqq\langle f,f\rangle_{L^{2}(\zeta)}^{1/2}\,. (D.1)

We write

L02​(ζ)≔{f∈L2​(ζ):∫f​𝑑ζ=0}.L_{0}^{2}(\zeta)\coloneqq\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\zeta):\int f\,\mathrm{d}\zeta=0\Bigr\}\,. (D.2)

When ζ=πη\zeta=\pi_{\eta}, we abbreviate the inner product and norm by ⟨f,g⟩\langle f,g\rangle and ‖f‖\|f\|.

Two functions equal ζ\zeta-almost everywhere represent the same vector. A closed linear subspace ℳ⊆L2​(ζ)\mathcal{M}\subseteq L^{2}(\zeta) has orthogonal complement ℳ⟂≔{g:⟨f,g⟩=0​ for all ​f∈ℳ}\mathcal{M}^{\perp}\coloneqq\{g:\langle f,g\rangle=0\text{ for all }f\in\mathcal{M}\}. Its orthogonal projection is the unique bounded operator 𝖯ℳ\mathsf{P}_{\mathcal{M}} for which 𝖯ℳ​f∈ℳ\mathsf{P}_{\mathcal{M}}f\in\mathcal{M} and f−𝖯ℳ​f∈ℳ⟂f-\mathsf{P}_{\mathcal{M}}f\in\mathcal{M}^{\perp}.

All operators in the convergence analysis are bounded linear operators on the indicated Hilbert spaces unless explicitly stated otherwise. The adjoint 𝖫∗\mathsf{L}^{*} is characterized by ⟨𝖫​f,g⟩=⟨f,𝖫∗​g⟩\langle\mathsf{L}f,g\rangle=\langle f,\mathsf{L}^{*}g\rangle. An operator is self-adjoint if 𝖫=𝖫∗\mathsf{L}=\mathsf{L}^{*}, a contraction if ‖𝖫​f‖≤‖f‖\|\mathsf{L}f\|\leq\|f\|, and unitary if it is onto and preserves norms. A self-adjoint involution, meaning 𝖫2=I\mathsf{L}^{2}=I, is unitary. For self-adjoint operators 𝖫1,𝖫2\mathsf{L}_{1},\mathsf{L}_{2},

𝖫1⪯𝖫2⟺⟨f,(𝖫2−𝖫1)f⟩≥0for every f\mathsf{L}_{1}\preceq\mathsf{L}_{2}\hskip 10.00002pt\Longleftrightarrow\hskip 10.00002pt\langle f,(\mathsf{L}_{2}-\mathsf{L}_{1})f\rangle\geq 0\hskip 10.00002pt\text{for every }f (D.3)

is the Loewner order. If 𝖫\mathsf{L} is self-adjoint, the spectral theorem defines ψ⁡(𝖫)\psi(\mathsf{L}) for bounded Borel functions ψ\psi; in particular 𝟏E​(𝖫)\mathbf{1}_{E}(\mathsf{L}) is the orthogonal projection onto the spectral set EE, and a non-negative operator has a unique non-negative square root.

Definition D.2 (Markov operators and density evolution).

Let 𝒦⁡(z,d​z′)\mathcal{K}(z,\mathrm{d}z^{\prime}) be a Markov kernel preserving ζ\zeta. Its Markov operator on observables is

(𝖪​f)​(z)≔∫f⁡(z′)​𝒦​(z,d​z′).(\mathsf{K}f)(z)\coloneqq\int f(z^{\prime})\,\mathcal{K}(z,\mathrm{d}z^{\prime})\,. (D.4)

It is a contraction on L2​(ζ)L^{2}(\zeta). Its adjoint 𝖪∗\mathsf{K}^{*} governs density evolution: if a law has density hh with respect to ζ\zeta, then its density after one step is 𝖪∗​h\mathsf{K}^{*}h. Constants are fixed by both operators.

If P≪ζP\ll\zeta has density hh, then

χ2(P∥ζ)=∥h−1∥ζ2.\chi^{2}(P\|\zeta)=\|h-1\|_{\zeta}^{2}\,. (D.5)

Consequently, an operator norm bound for 𝖪\mathsf{K} on L02​(ζ)L_{0}^{2}(\zeta) gives the same bound for its adjoint 𝖪∗\mathsf{K}^{*}, and hence gives χ2\chi^{2} contraction.
